lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Did they feed you on that plane?
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, interrogating, bossy] Did they FEED you on that plane?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It was Delta One, Mom. They fed me twice.
lines.script: [bragging] It was Delta ONE, Mom. [proud] They fed me twice.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Twice! You must be starving!
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, alarmed] TWICE! [warm Long Island accent, punchline, fussing] You must be starving!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Wait, I have to show you something first. A hill in Los Angeles stood up, talked to us, and sneezed this at me.
lines.script: [bursting to tell] Wait, I have to show you something first. [storytelling, building] A hill in Los Angeles stood up, talked to us, and... [disbelief] SNEEZED this at me.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: A hill stood up? Out there too? First my kitchen, now California!
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, alarmed] A hill stood up? [warm Long Island accent, indignant] Out there TOO? [warm Long Island accent, taking it personally] First my kitchen, now California!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That's gold like my teeth! Cozy Rosie has one, and now you have one. Where's mine?
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, thrilled] That's gold like my teeth! [thick New York accent, tallying] Cozy Rosie has one, and now you have one. [thick New York accent, punchline, complaining] Where's MINE?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: You have to get it from a monster, Boppy.
lines.script: [explaining the rules] You have to get it from a MONSTER, Boppy.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Then I know just the fish. The Whisker Perch. Whiskers like a cat. I saw him at Cattail Pier in 1994, and he was THIS big.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, bragging] Then I know just the fish. [thick New York accent, storytelling] The Whisker Perch. Whiskers like a cat. [thick New York accent, exaggerating, slowly] I saw him at Cattail Pier in 1994, and he was... THIS big.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Last time he was only THIS big.
lines.script: [catching him out] Last time he was only THIS big.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: He grew. It's been thirty years.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, defensive] He GREW. [thick New York accent, justifying] It's been thirty years.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: We believe you now, Boppy. You were right about the Big One.
lines.script: [sincere, making amends] We believe you now, Boppy. [admitting] You were RIGHT about the Big One.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Say that again, slower. Deary, are you hearing this?
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, savoring it] Say that again... SLOWER. [thick New York accent, gloating, calling out] Deary, are you hearing this?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: I heard it. Don't let it go to your head. Your hat won't fit.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, unimpressed] I heard it. [warm Long Island accent, warning] Don't let it go to your head. [warm Long Island accent, punchline, deadpan] Your hat won't fit.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I believe every fish story you ever told me. I'm bringing the big net.
lines.script: [sincere] I believe every fish story you EVER told me. [eager] I'm bringing the big net.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mom, there's one more thing. There was a lemon frozen inside an orange block, just like the dragonfly. And this was lying under it.
lines.script: [serious] Mom, there's one more thing. [explaining carefully] There was a lemon frozen inside an orange block, just like the dragonfly. [uneasy] And THIS was lying under it.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Same bulb. One at my pond and one three thousand miles away.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, recognizing, uneasy] Same bulb. [warm Long Island accent, working it out] One at my pond... and one three THOUSAND miles away.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Two thousand four hundred and seventy-five.
lines.script: [correcting, automatic] Two thousand four hundred and seventy-five.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tom. Not now.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, shutting him down] Tom. Not now.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: I don't know what this is and I don't like it. They're both going in the drawer, and all four of you are coming home in one piece. That's not a request.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, admitting, uneasy] I don't know what this is and I don't LIKE it. [warm Long Island accent, giving orders] They're both going in the drawer, and all four of you are coming home in one piece. [warm Long Island accent, final, firm] That's not a request.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You said next time you were coming.
lines.script: [reminding, teasing] You said NEXT time you were coming.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Stomach or no stomach. Let's go fishing!
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, vowing] Stomach or no stomach. [thick New York accent, rallying, thrilled] Let's go FISHING!

lines.speaker: Oolong
lines.text: The kettle says there was a big flash over the marsh this morning. Like lightning, but with no thunder and no rain.
lines.script: [gossiping, hushed] The kettle says there was a big flash over the marsh this morning. [mysterious] Like lightning... but with NO thunder and no rain.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A flash! The fish at the pond said that. So did the hill!
lines.script: [alarmed, recognizing] A flash! [connecting it] The fish at the pond said that. So did the HILL!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Lightning over my marsh? If anybody's frying that perch, it's me.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, territorial] Lightning over MY marsh? [thick New York accent, punchline, joking] If anybody's frying that perch, it's me.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I've got the tackle box in one hand and the big net in the other. I'm ready.
lines.script: [whispering, reporting for duty] I've got the tackle box in one hand and the big net in the other. [proud] I'm READY.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Those are WHISKERS! That's him! That's the Whisker Perch! Old Iron-Gill himself!
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, shouting, thrilled] Those are WHISKERS! That's him! [thick New York accent, announcing] That's the Whisker Perch! [thick New York accent, reverent] Old Iron-Gill himself!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy, he's way bigger than THIS big. He's bigger than the pier!
lines.script: [amazed] Boppy, he's way bigger than THIS big. [disbelief] He's bigger than the PIER!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I TOLD everybody he grew!
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, gloating, shouting] I TOLD everybody he grew!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: He TALKS? Thirty years I've been talking to that fish, and NOW he answers?
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, disbelief] He TALKS? [thick New York accent, punchline, offended] Thirty years I've been talking to that fish, and NOW he answers?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boppy, that's what the Big One was like! Now you saw one too!
lines.script: [excited, including him] Boppy, that's what the Big One was like! [delighted] Now YOU saw one too!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I saw one! And Deedee is going to believe me. That's worse. She'll want details.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, triumphant] I SAW one! And Deedee is going to believe me... [thick New York accent, realizing, dreading] That's worse. [thick New York accent, punchline, worried] She'll want details.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: A talking sock! All my life I've been losing socks, and THIS is where they go?
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, amazed] A talking SOCK! [thick New York accent, punchline, indignant] All my life I've been losing socks, and THIS is where they go?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Excuse me, Mr. Sock. We haven't seen your other sock. We're very sorry.
lines.script: [overly polite] Excuse me, Mr. Sock. [informing, earnest] We haven't seen your other sock. [apologizing sincerely] We're VERY sorry.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy, were YOU the one who cast it badly in 1997?
lines.script: [catching him out, sly] Boppy, were YOU the one who cast it badly in 1997?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: It was windy. Write that down. It was very windy.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, defensive] It was windy. [thick New York accent, ordering] Write that down. [thick New York accent, insisting, slowly] It was... VERY windy.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The old reeds. I played back in there when I was nine. There's a sundial in a clearing. We called it Sundial Hollow.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, remembering, fond] The old reeds. I played back in there when I was nine. [thick New York accent, storytelling] There's a sundial in a clearing. [thick New York accent, wistful] We called it Sundial Hollow.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He means please. Could you please shove over?
lines.script: [translating, polite] He means please. [overly polite] Could you... PLEASE shove over?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That's my boot! I lost that boot in 1988!
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, recognizing, thrilled] That's my BOOT! [thick New York accent, amazed] I lost that boot in 1988!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: This is Sundial Hollow. I haven't been back here since I was nine.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, quiet, remembering] This is Sundial Hollow. [thick New York accent, wistful] I haven't been back here since I was nine.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: It was green. All of this was green. Who took the green out of my hollow?
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, hurt, quiet] It was green. [thick New York accent, insisting] ALL of this was green. [thick New York accent, bewildered, slowly] Who took the green out of my hollow?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata! There's a fish in the SKY!
lines.script: [shrieking] Tata! [pointing it out] There's a fish in the SKY!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's inside an orange block, like the dragonfly. It's just hanging there. Nothing is holding it up!
lines.script: [investigating, quick] It's inside an orange block, like the dragonfly. It's just hanging there. [disbelief] NOTHING is holding it up!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That fish jumped, and he never came down. Seventy-some years I've been fishing, and I never saw a fish stay up.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, hushed, awed] That fish jumped, and he never came down. [thick New York accent, reverent, slowly] Seventy-some years I've been fishing, and I never saw a fish... stay UP.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Tom. Get under it with the net.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, giving an order] Tom. Get under it with the net.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It can't be moved. I tried one at the pond and one in California.
lines.script: [reasoning, careful] It can't be moved. [informing] I tried one at the pond AND one in California.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Then it won't hurt to hold the net.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, punchline, bossy] Then it won't HURT to hold the net.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I'm holding the net.
lines.script: [obeying, flat] I'm holding the net.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Good. Hold it better.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, approving] Good... [thick New York accent, punchline, bossy] Hold it BETTER.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: There's a little round hole in the side, like the dragonfly one had. I'm drawing it.
lines.script: [investigating] There's a little round hole in the side, like the dragonfly one had. [businesslike] I'm drawing it.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: And there's Deedee's litter! On the clock rock!
lines.script: [tattling, proud] And there's Deedee's LITTER! On the clock rock!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dragonfly: grey grass, orange block, round hole, burnt bulb. Fish: grey reeds, orange block, round hole, burnt bulb.
lines.script: [reading her notes, precise] Dragonfly: grey grass, orange block, round hole, burnt bulb. [comparing] Fish: grey reeds, orange block, round hole, burnt bulb.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Lemon: grey tree, orange block, round hole, burnt bulb.
lines.script: [adding, quiet] Lemon: grey tree, orange block, round hole, burnt bulb.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I'm writing that down too. In pen.
lines.script: [serious] I'm writing that down too. [punchline, firm] In PEN.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Somebody want to tell me what it means?
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, lost, asking] Somebody want to tell me what it MEANS?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I don't know yet, Boppy. I'm only on page two.
lines.script: [admitting] I don't know yet, Boppy. [punchline, honest] I'm only on page two.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Well, it's a small one anyway. Mine was double.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, dismissing, bragging] Well, it's a SMALL one anyway. [thick New York accent, exaggerating] Mine was double.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That's the Deep Pool. That's where Iron-Gill goes to sulk. Tom, you can put the net down.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, alert, serious] That's the Deep Pool. [thick New York accent, explaining] That's where Iron-Gill goes to sulk. [thick New York accent, punchline, kindly] Tom, you can put the net down.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: This morning there was a flash over the hollow. Now I'm big enough to come up and say it to your face.
lines.script: [deep, hurt] This morning there was a flash over the hollow. [confronting] Now I'm big enough to come up and say it to your FACE.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: And he has gold in his mustache!
lines.script: [pointing it out, shrill] And he has GOLD in his mustache!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: First the Big One asks about me, and now this one. I'm very big with the fish, Tom.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, flattered] First the Big One asks about me, and now this one. [thick New York accent, punchline, bragging] I'm VERY big with the fish, Tom.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You're a celebrity. I'll hold the net.
lines.script: [humoring him] You're a celebrity. [punchline, dutiful] I'll hold the net.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Tom. Tackle box. We do this the old way.
lines.script: [serious, taking charge] Tom. Tackle box. [determined] We do this the OLD way.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: And take this. It's been itching my mustache all day.
lines.script: [deep, offering] And take this. [complaining] It's been itching my mustache ALL day.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Gold like my teeth, with a fish on it! I got one! Cozy Rosie, I got one!
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, overjoyed, shouting] Gold like my teeth, with a FISH on it! [thick New York accent, gloating] I got one! Cozy Rosie, I got one!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boppy got treasure! Now your mouth matches your hat!
lines.script: [cheering] Boppy got treasure! [punchline, teasing] Now your mouth matches your HAT!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Put the date. Put the time. And put that he was THIS big.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, dictating] Put the date. Put the time. [thick New York accent, exaggerating] And put that he was... THIS big.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy, he was bigger than that.
lines.script: [correcting, dry] Boppy, he was BIGGER than that.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: First time in my life I ever undersold a fish.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, amazed at himself] First time in my life I ever... [thick New York accent, punchline] UNDERSOLD a fish.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Still up there. Somebody ought to let that fish finish his jump.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, quiet, noticing] Still up there. [thick New York accent, tender] Somebody ought to let that fish finish his jump.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Old Iron-Gill. Forty years, Deary. I TOLD everybody.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, announcing, proud] Old Iron-Gill. [thick New York accent, gloating] Forty years, Deary. I TOLD everybody.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I have proof. It's in my notebook. I drew his mustache.
lines.script: [backing him up] I have proof. It's in my notebook. [proud] I drew his MUSTACHE.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Thank you, Cozy Rosie. Now. Let me look at him.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, thanking, warm] Thank you, Cozy Rosie. [warm Long Island accent, taking over, sharp] Now. Let me look at him.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Look. I got gold. From the fish.
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, showing off, hopeful] Look. I got gold. From the FISH.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Fifty-one years I've been married to you, hubby, and you never once brought ME gold from a fish.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, teasing, dry] Fifty-one years I've been married to you, hubby, and you never once brought... ME gold from a fish.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: It's gold like my teeth!
lines.script: [deep voice, thick New York accent, bragging] It's gold like my TEETH!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: I paid for those teeth.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, punchline, deadpan] I PAID for those teeth.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Deedee, there's another orange block. There's a fish in it, and it's stuck up in the air over the water.
lines.script: [reporting, serious] Deedee, there's another orange block. [explaining carefully] There's a fish in it, and it's stuck up in the AIR over the water.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: And more litter.
lines.script: [tattling, matter-of-fact] And more litter.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Three. My pond, California, and the marsh.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, counting, grim] Three. [warm Long Island accent, listing, slowly] My pond, California, and the marsh.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: New rule. Nobody in this family goes anywhere alone. Not to the pond, not to the pier, not to the mailbox. Tom, that goes for Los Angeles too.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, laying down the law] New rule. Nobody in this family goes anywhere ALONE. [warm Long Island accent, listing, firm] Not to the pond, not to the pier, not to the mailbox. [warm Long Island accent, pointed, loving] Tom, that goes for Los Angeles too.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Yes, Mom.
lines.script: [obeying, quiet] Yes, Mom.
